Widgetry Merit Badge

Overview

Short lead.

The Widgetry merit badge introduces Scouts to the design, safe assembly, and repair of widgets, from the simplest hand-turned kind to the geared assemblies that show up in everyday machinery. Scouts who earn it learn to work carefully with tools and to explain what they built to someone else.

From Scout Life

Van Horn likes to connect requirement 4 with requirement 7 when he teaches this badge at summer camp.

Widgetry Merit Badge Requirements

The requirements will be fed dynamically using the Scoutbook integration.

The previous version of the merit badge requirements can be found in the 2024 printing.

1. Widget safety. Do the following:
a. Explain the hazards you are most likely to encounter while working with widgets, and what you should do to anticipate, mitigate, prevent, and respond to these hazards.
b. Show that you know first aid for the injuries that could occur while widgeting, including:

(1) Pinched fingers

(2) Eye irritation from widget dust

(3) Minor cuts and scrapes

2. Do the following:
a. Describe the three classes of widget and give an example of each.
b. Explain to your counselor how a widget differs from a gadget.

  1. 3. Design a widget of your own. Then do the following:
    1. a. Sketch your design and label its working parts.
    2. b. Build your widget and demonstrate that it works as designed.

4. Visit a widget works, a repair shop, or a maker space. Report to your counselor on what you saw being made and how the work was organized.

Resources: Widget Safety Guide (No. 33216), Widget World magazine index

Ask your counselor which of these is current before you rely on it.

5. Find out about three career opportunities in widgetry. Then do the following:

a. Pick one and find out the education, training, and experience it requires.

b. Discuss with your counselor whether this profession might interest you.
